record.field: Work Inbox — what is waiting for me
Built here as a read-only prototype. It is not the landing screen, and nothing is approved from it.
One screen answering “what is waiting for me?” — claims to certify, cheques to sign, bills to review, expenses to approve, unmatched bank lines — instead of opening eight apps to find out.

Open it from Preview › Working Prototypes and judge the thing itself rather than the description. Making it the landing screen is easy; letting approvals happen on it is the part that needs your decision, because an approval taken outside the document's own form has no audit trail unless it is wired through the document.
A screen per role, not one dashboard
No dashboards at all today. Every role opens the same menus.

A general manager screen (contract value, receivables, cash, warnings), a finance screen (work in progress, cost at completion, retention, VAT, closing), and a project manager screen with no accounting on it at all.

Agreed on the project manager screen — he should not see the ledger, and the access rights already allow that today. I would not build three dashboards of figures: the inbox plus one exception list per role carries the same information and does not go stale. A dashboard is the first thing that stops being maintained, and a stale dashboard is worse than none.
One button that names the next step
Documents have their state buttons, and Complete All runs the whole chain. Neither tells the user which single step comes next.

Draft → quantity check → sequence check → project manager → finance → invoice → collection, with one button relabelled at each stage: Send for review, then Approve, then Create invoice, then Record collection.

The cheapest of the experience items and the one your complaint was really about. One caution: keep it separate from Complete All. A button that names one step teaches the workflow; a button that does seven hides it, and the person who never learned the sequence is the person who cannot tell when it went wrong.
A stepped wizard for the progress claim

The claim already pulls the bill of quantities, carries previous quantities forward, and refuses over-measurement and out-of-order certification. What is missing is only the step-by-step presentation.
Project → period → lines extracted → enter current quantities → the system computes previous + current = cumulative and runs its checks → create the claim.

Worth doing, but it is presentation, not protection. The checks are what stop a wrong claim, and they already exist and are enforced when the claim is saved, not when a wizard asks nicely. I would rank the claim form's own clarity — quantity, previous, cumulative, remaining in one grid — ahead of the wizard, and the wizard after the change order.
Smart defaults, and a warning before posting

Currency, tax, emirate and the fiscal position are already derived from the customer. Project, cost centre and payment terms are not, and missing data is refused at posting instead of warned about while the invoice is open.
Choosing the customer fills in everything derivable, and anything missing shows on the form as a warning: this customer has no emirate — set it before posting.

The emirate is the proof of why this matters: every customer in this database lacked one, so a non-UAE fiscal position was zero-rating domestic sales until it was found and fixed. A warning while the invoice is still open costs under a day and prevents exactly that class of error — the kind nobody notices until the return is filed.
The rules are real and enforced, but each lives in the module that owns its document.

One module holding the conditions — cumulative quantity not above the bill unless a change order is approved, the previous certificate posted, retention, tax position, revenue recognition — instead of six modules each holding their own.

I would share the check functions and stop there, rather than make the rules configurable. These rules come from UAE law and from IFRS 15: they must be identical for every client, and a rules table invites a client to switch off the one refusing their claim. Shared functions give you the single place to edit without that risk — the benefit you actually described.
A confidence score for bank matching
Matching is built and automatic, but its answer is yes or no. A weak match and a certain one are treated the same.

98% invoice number and amount both match · 92% the party's only open document of exactly this amount · 88% a reconciliation rule claims it · 63% document named, amount differs · 12% nothing recognised. Settle automatically above 95% and send the rest to the inbox.

Working now in Preview › Bank Match Confidence, scored against the open lines in this database. This is the item I would build first: it changes nothing about whether the ledger is correct and everything about how a thousand lines a month get handled. Note the threshold is a policy, not a constant — you own it, and it should be visible in settings.
Nothing exists. An advance to staff is an ordinary journal entry, with nothing tracking what is left of it.

Request → approval → payment → spending → receipts → settlement → balance → return, with the balance visible (Ahmed: 10,000 advanced, 7,200 spent, 2,800 outstanding) and a new advance refused while an old one is unsettled, except under a specific right.

This is the largest genuine hole in the system for a contractor. Site cash moves through advances, and an unsettled advance is a receivable nobody can age — it sits in a control account and grows. It also gives the expense module a reason to exist beyond reimbursement, which is how the receipts arrive at all.
A change order that actually changes the contract

A variation order exists, with value, cost impact, margin and an approval state. It does not touch the bill of quantities, carries no time impact, no attachments and no record of who requested it, and approving it does not revise the contract value or the budget.

The order carries the original line, the original and new quantity, the price, the financial and the time impact, attachments, correspondence, who asked, who approved, and when. Approving it updates the bill of quantities, the contract value, the budget, the cost at completion and revenue recognition.

This is the item that decides whether the product is a contracting system. The claim already refuses to measure more than the bill allows; without a change order that raises the bill, that refusal becomes the thing users work around — and the moment they work around it, the quantities stop meaning anything and so does the percentage of completion built on them.
Commitments and cost at completion, side by side
The figures exist and are computed — committed, cost at completion, over budget, forecast loss. What is missing is a screen that puts them side by side instead of as columns inside one contract form.
Budget 10M, actual 4M, committed 3M, remaining 3M — and above all cost at completion 11.2M with a red 1.2M expected overrun, shown before the overrun happens rather than reported after it.

Already visible in Preview › Project Health for every live contract, one row each. Since the arithmetic is done and tested, this is a view rather than a feature — which is why I recommend it even though the work is under a day.
Project health, with reasons instead of a score
Every condition is computed somewhere. Nothing gathered them into one row per project until this prototype did.

One row per project: contract, budget, actual, committed, cost at completion, overrun, forecast margin, percent by cost against percent measured, certified, collected, outstanding — and a plain list of what needs attention.

I followed your own advice and left the aggregate score out. A number a manager can neither argue with nor act on is worse than three sentences he can. The screen says over budget by 8.4 percent, claim certified and not invoiced, collection behind — and each of those names the next move.
A site engineer screen on the phone
Nothing. An engineer given access today gets the whole back office on a phone screen.
My projects, then: raise a claim, upload a receipt, request materials, record labour, request a purchase, attach a photo, ask for a change order, site note, problem, leave, attendance.

Agreed that this is what sells the product, and agreed with building it on Odoo's own field service, tasks and barcode capabilities instead of a separate platform. But it is a week or more, and it depends on the site store and employee advances existing first: an engineer requesting materials against nothing is a form that goes nowhere.
The system does not use inventory at all. Material reaches a job only as a supplier bill.

Main warehouse → site → engineer → issue request → approval → issue, posting itself to cost centre, cost code and project: 120 bags of cement, villa project, concrete item, direct cost — with no accountant typing a journal entry.

Material bought is not material consumed, and today the system cannot tell the difference: a delivery to the yard is charged to whichever project the bill names. That overstates completion on one job and understates it on another — the same error the percentage-of-completion revenue is calculated from, which is why this matters more than it looks.
Month-end closing wizard, and a period lock

The checks exist as a script nobody runs and, now, as a screen. There is no guided close and no period lock, and the year-end closing module is half installed on the old demo database and will not upgrade.

Press Start closing, and the system checks drafts, uncertified claims, costs with no cost centre or cost code, unmatched bank lines, VAT, work in progress, retention, accruals, prepayments, customer and vendor advances, payroll, pending cheques and expiring guarantees — then says 11 problems, opens each one, and when they are gone: month ready to close, lock period.

Preview › Month-End Readiness already runs those checks against this database and shows only what blocks the close. The lock is the part that matters most and the part not built: without it a posted month keeps changing, and the statements you sent the bank stop matching the statements in the system — which is the one thing an auditor will find.

Thirty-seven sensitive fields are tracked, and every change sits in the chatter with the user, the old value and the new one. What is missing is a reason attached to the change, and one screen that reads across documents.
Contract value 10,000,000 → 10,500,000, user CFO, reason: approved change order CO-004, 27/09/2026 14:35 — for claims, contracts, change orders, journal entries, cheques, taxes and access rights.

The tracking is there; the reason is not, and the reason is the only part an auditor ever asks about. Ask for it at the moment of the change — a field on the form, refused if empty — and the trail turns from a log into evidence. Reading it across documents is the easy half and can follow.
An assistant that reads and explains, and never posts

What is the expected cost of the villa project? Which claims are certified and not invoiced? Why did the school project's margin fall? Which invoices are more than 30 days overdue? Answered from the data. Later, limited actions that only ever produce a draft.

I agree completely with the limit — never post, pay or approve without a person — and I would go further. Three of the four questions listed there are answered by screens in this app, cheaply and identically every time, which a language model cannot promise. Build the assistant when the screens exist and people still cannot find the answer, not instead of them.
A send button exists on invoices and statements. There is no record that it was sent, no automatic reminder, and no switch to turn it off for one client.
On issue: send the invoice, the link, the number, the amount and the due date; record it as sent, later as paid; remind after 7 days and again after 14. Switchable off per client.

The reminder is the valuable half, and the sending is already built. One condition, which is why I mark it for your decision rather than doing it: reminders go out on a schedule with nobody watching, so they must be off by default and turned on per customer. A second reminder to a client the company is mid-negotiation with costs more than the collection it chases.

Attachments work, and guarantees have an expiry date with a warning. Nothing groups a contract's, a supplier's or a project's documents, and licences and trade certificates have no expiry date at all.

Under the contract: the original, addenda, change orders, correspondence, claims, guarantees, cheques. Under the supplier: contract, licence, TRN, bank certificate, cheques, invoices. Under the project: bill of quantities, drawings, site reports, certificates, invoices, photos. With alerts — the licence expires in 20 days.

The expiry dates are the reason to build it. Grouping files is a convenience; an expired supplier licence found during an audit, or a guarantee that lapsed while a claim was outstanding, is money. Model the dates first and the folders second — the folders are what makes it look finished, the dates are what makes it worth having.
Heavy work moved to the background
Everything runs inside the request. The server is still in threaded mode with no workers configured, so a large import holds the page and a second user waits behind it.

Bank statement imports, Excel imports, large reports, payment runs, mass journal entries, service provider sync, bulk notifications and work-in-progress reports move to a job queue. OCA's queue_job supports Odoo 18 and requires more than one worker.

Correct that this is architecture rather than polish: the workers must be set before a second client shares the server, and that is a production setting still sitting at its default. I would configure the workers now, today, and add the queue when an import actually times out — the first is an hour, the second is a week.
Performance monitoring, and a load-test database
Nothing is measured. The hosting sizing in the architecture report is an estimate and says so.

Screen open time, SQL queries, slow requests, cron and queue duration, user count, worker state, server errors and database size — plus a synthetic database (100 projects, 50,000 invoices, 500,000 journal lines, 100,000 bank transactions) measured at 5, 10, 20 and 30 users.

The load-test database is the half I would build first and it is cheap: generating it is a script, and it replaces a guess about hosting with a measurement. Monitoring can wait for the first client who complains, because until there is a baseline there is nothing to compare a measurement against.
Built. Client, database, plan, users against the limit, size, last activity, backup state, health with its reason, and a renewal warning — for every tenant.
A table of every tenant database with size, users, backup and health, so one person can run ten clients.
Nothing to decide: open Platform › Tenants and look. What it does not yet carry is the module version each client runs, which is the next proposal in this list.
No tenant record says which version it runs, so an upgrade is done by hand and remembered by hand.
Every release numbered, with migration scripts, tests, database compatibility and a rollback plan; then per client: current 1.4.1, available 1.4.2 → back up → run tests → upgrade → health check.

The version field and the rollback plan are worth doing before the third client, not after. The one-click upgrade can wait; the record of who runs what cannot, because the first question on any support call is which version they are on — and today the only way to answer it is to log into their database.
Backup verification by actually restoring it
Backups run and are recorded with size, duration and errors, and the restore manifest is written. No backup has ever been restored to prove that it can be.
Weekly: back up → restore into a temporary environment → health check → destroy it, and show last verified restore: 27 Sep 2026.

I agree this is a condition rather than a feature. A backup that has never been restored is a file, not a backup, and the health check that would run against the restored copy already exists — so the work is mostly wiring. This is the one item on the list I would not let a client go live without.
Individual warnings exist — guarantee expiring, over budget, over the user limit — each written into the code that owns it. There are no rules, no recipients and no channels.

Project cost above 90% of budget → project manager. Cost at completion above the contract → finance. Guarantee under 30 days → finance. Customer over 30 days late → accounts. Cheque bounced → finance and the general manager. Advance overdue → HR and finance. Each with its channel: in the system, email, WhatsApp, push.

Here a rules table earns its place, unlike the business rules: who is told, at what threshold, on which channel is genuinely a company's own choice and changes without a developer. Start in the system only, and add email and WhatsApp once somebody complains they missed one — an alert nobody reads trains people to ignore the next one.
UAE tax as master data, not code
The taxes and the fiscal positions are configuration already. But the city-to-emirate map is a Python dictionary I wrote, and you cannot add a city to it.

A table of emirate, fiscal position, VAT treatment, whether a TRN is required, default accounts and rules — editable without touching Python. Plus an e-invoicing adapter, so the product is not tied to one accredited service provider.

The hardcoded map is a fair criticism of my own work: a customer in a town that dictionary does not list silently ends up with no emirate, which is the exact failure that zero-rated domestic sales here. Moving it to a table is under a day. The adapter I agree with entirely — the federal programme and the accredited provider list are still changing, and the PINT AE document is already written independently of any provider.
Structured data first, PDF never the source
This is already the rule. Bank statements import from CSV, XLSX and CAMT and are matched automatically; PDF was refused deliberately.
CSV, XLSX, API, XML, Peppol, bank feeds — and PDF only as something to read or attach, never the source of truth when a structured format exists.

Nothing to decide, but worth recording as a policy rather than a coincidence, because the request to import PDF statements will come back. A machine that reads a PDF correctly 98 percent of the time is wrong once every fifty lines, in a ledger that has to tie to the fils.
Odoo searches inside whichever list is open. Typing an invoice number does not show you the claim, the payment and the entry behind it.

Type INV/2026/00005 and get the invoice, the customer, the claim, the account, the payment, the entry and the bank line. Type the villa project and get the contract, bill of quantities, budget, invoices, bills, expenses, retention, work in progress and change orders.

Useful, and less small than it looks: a search across models either queries a dozen tables on every keystroke or needs an index that has to be maintained. The contract form already carries the project half of this. I would put the links on the documents themselves — an invoice showing its claim, a claim showing its invoice — and leave the search bar as Odoo built it.
Odoo 18 ships one. Ctrl+K opens it and it already searches menus, records and commands. Our own actions are simply not registered in it.
Press Ctrl+K and type create invoice, or open the villa project, or approve claim 7, or bank.

Try it before approving anything — the feature is in the product you already have. What is worth an hour is registering our own commands in it and checking it behaves in Arabic. Building a second palette would mean maintaining what Odoo maintains for us.
Complete All already runs over a selection. Assigning a cost centre or a project to fifty lines at once, and sending in bulk, do not exist.
Approve, reject, set cost centre, set project, export, send by WhatsApp, send by email, post — over everything selected.

Setting the cost centre in bulk is the one that pays for itself: the data quality screen finds costs with no cost centre, and fixing them one at a time is why they stay unfixed. Bulk posting I would leave out — posting fifty entries on one click is fifty entries nobody read, and that is the complaint about Complete All in a new place.
Data quality as a screen, not a report
Built here as a screen over the same checks the script used to print. The fix-everything-automatically button is not built.
11 problems — projects 3, customers 1, vendors 2, expenses 5 — then: fix all automatically, or review.

Open Preview › Data Quality: the screen is there, every row counts real records in this database and opens them. I recommend against fix all. What would it fix? A cost with no cost centre has no correct answer the system can guess, and a guessed cost centre moves money to the wrong project while reporting the problem as solved — the worst of the two outcomes. Bulk assignment with a person choosing saves the same hours honestly.
Not built, and not proposed to be.
Activity networks, logic links, float, resource levelling and a baseline programme against which delay is claimed.
Agreed with excluding it. That is a different product, and the contractors who need it already own it. What is worth taking from it is one field — the time impact on a change order — not the engine.
Not built, and not proposed to be.
A chart of accounts, tax regime and statutory reports for more than one country.

Agreed. The product's value is that it knows the UAE rules exactly — VAT per emirate, Form 201, the federal e-invoicing programme. Generalising that away is how the advantage is lost, and Odoo already localises other countries for whoever needs them.
Reading bank statements out of PDF
Extracting transactions from a PDF statement by character recognition.

Agreed, and this one I would refuse rather than defer. Every UAE bank offers CSV or XLSX; choosing the harder input to save the customer one menu click means the ledger's bank balance comes from character recognition. The import already takes CSV, XLSX and CAMT.
An AI that posts entries and makes payments
Not built, and it should stay that way.
An assistant permitted to post journal entries, pay suppliers and approve documents on its own.

Agreed, and I would keep it refused permanently rather than scheduled for later. The audit trail has to name a person for every posting; an assistant that posts breaks the single property that makes a ledger evidence.
Not built, and not proposed to be.
A report for every question anyone has ever asked, added to the reporting menu.

Agreed. The reporting menu was flattened for exactly this reason, and your complaint was that you could not find anything in it. An exception screen tells you what needs you; eighty reports tell you to go looking.
